intro: Book the Audit, detail 1 of 4. Only the heading changes. 14 lines that passed the gates (true of the audit as /pilot describes it, no result promised; a question allowed as a single close), scored on the second sheet, the best three beside today.

lists.name: Today
rows: Got a job everyone hates doing?
lists.note: The owner’s words, a question that makes them think of one job. Says nothing about what they get.

lists.name: 1. The page
rows: Your worst jobs, on one page.
lists.note: What they walk away with, made physical: the written page with the three jobs costing them most. Recommended.

lists.name: 2. Book it, keep it
rows: Book the audit. Keep the page.
lists.note: Two beats; the second is the reassurance that the page is theirs either way.

lists.name: 3. The hand-over
rows: Which job would you hand over first?
lists.note: The audit’s own question, so the owner names a job before booking.

test.intro: Every line that passed the gates, scored and sorted. Mark the numbers that grab you and any that put you off.
test.key: Scale: 0 to 5, one point each, half for partly. Picture, Prove and Only us are Harry Dry’s three questions; Device is one structural move; Your shape is short, one claim, no tail, from your picks (writing-style references/lines.md).

rows.line: Your worst jobs, on one page.
rows.why: What the owner walks away with, made physical: the written page with the three jobs costing them most. True, and only an audit like this one gives it.

rows.line: Book the audit. Keep the page.
rows.why: Two beats, the second the reassurance (the page is yours either way).

rows.line: Your worst job has a price. Find it.
rows.why: Surprise then a command; a beat long.

rows.line: Which job would you hand over first?
rows.why: A question that is the audit’s own question; makes the owner name one.

rows.line: Got a job everyone hates doing?
rows.why: Today. The owner’s words and a question that makes them think of one; says nothing about what they get.

rows.line: Forty five minutes. One page. Your worst jobs, priced.
rows.why: A three with the facts in it; repeats the list under it.

rows.line: The job everyone hates, priced in your figures.
rows.why: The audit’s result in the owner’s money; long.

rows.line: Hand over the job everyone hates.
rows.why: An order; jumps to the pilot before the audit.

rows.line: Free to find out. Yours to keep.
rows.why: Two beats about the terms; nothing to picture.

rows.line: One job. Forty five minutes. A page back.
rows.why: A three; “one job” undersells the three jobs the page names.
A picture (eating) and a question; any consultant could ask it.

rows.line: Which job is costing you most?
rows.why: Plain question; less of a picture than the hand-over one.

rows.line: Start with the job that costs you most.
rows.why: How It Works’s heading, so the page repeats itself.
Echoes the hero; “starts here” is a stock phrase.
